title: STPA / STAMP vocabulary as a declared OKF domain pack
honestBoundary: The analysis is AUTHORED; the platform CHECKS it. Modelwrite does not perform STPA, does not infer hazards from a design, and never claims to.
howToRead: Every STPA concept is expressed as an existing OKF node kind (block, signal, requirement) carrying a declared stereotype, and every STPA relationship is an existing OKF edge kind (triggers, dependency, reference). No engine change is required to hold this vocabulary; the completeness checks are computed over the resulting typed graph.

nodeKinds.meaning: a thing: a component, a state, an analysis artifact
an information flow: a command or a reading
a system-level constraint or requirement the design must satisfy

edgeKinds.meaning: a directional flow: a controller issues a command, a process returns a reading
a traceability claim: a hazard is mitigated by a constraint, an element satisfies a constraint
an analysis artifact names the thing it is about: a UCA names its control action, a loss scenario names its UCA

stereotypes.name: Loss
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A system-level loss to be prevented (loss of life, loss of aircraft, loss of mission).
stereotypes.note: The top of the losses -> hazards -> constraints chain; authored, never inferred.

stereotypes.name: Hazard
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A system state or condition that, together with a worst-case set of environmental conditions, leads to a loss.
stereotypes.note: Linked to the system-level constraints that mitigate it by a dependency edge labelled Mitigate.

stereotypes.name: SystemConstraint
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A system-level constraint (a safety requirement) the design must enforce.
stereotypes.note: A constraint is a requirement: its coverage by the design is already computed by the platform's requirement-coverage check (Satisfy / Refine / Verify / Allocate).

stereotypes.name: Controller
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A component that provides control actions and enforces constraints over the process it controls.

stereotypes.name: ControlledProcess
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: The process under the controller's control; it returns feedback about its state.

stereotypes.name: ControlAction
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A command the controller issues to the controlled process.
stereotypes.note: A control action is a named signal node so a UCA analysis can reference it by id. The control loop flows Controller --triggers--> ControlAction --triggers--> ControlledProcess.

stereotypes.name: Feedback
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: Information the controlled process returns to the controller about its state.
stereotypes.note: Feedback is a named signal node; the loop closes ControlledProcess --triggers--> Feedback --triggers--> Controller. A controller with a control action but no feedback path is the classic defect.

stereotypes.name: UnsafeControlAction
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A control action that, in a particular context, leads to a hazard.
stereotypes.note: A UCA node carries TWO stereotypes: UnsafeControlAction plus exactly one UCA type token from ucaTypes. It references its control action with a reference edge (UCA --reference--> ControlAction).

stereotypes.name: LossScenario
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A causal scenario explaining how a UCA could occur and lead to a hazard.
stereotypes.note: References the UCA it explains with a reference edge (LossScenario --reference--> UCA).

stereotypes.name: CausalFactor
stereotypes.stpaMeaning: A factor that contributes to a loss scenario.
stereotypes.note: Referenced from its loss scenario with a reference edge (LossScenario --reference--> CausalFactor).

ucaTypes.meaning: the control action is not provided when it is needed
the control action is provided when it should not be, or is unsafe in the context
the control action is provided too early, too late, or in the wrong order
the control action is stopped too soon or applied too long

edges.relation: hazard is mitigated by a system-level constraint
edges.label: Mitigate

edges.relation: a design element satisfies a constraint
edges.label: Satisfy / Refine / Verify / Allocate (existing coverage)

edges.relation: a UCA analyses a control action
a loss scenario explains a UCA
a loss scenario has a causal factor

checks.summary: every ControlAction must have a UCA for each of the four UCA types
a Controller with a ControlAction must have a feedback path
every Hazard must be mitigated by a constraint; every constraint must reach the design
every UCA must be explained by a loss scenario
the same counts, per commit on a branch
